# EMET — Gospel of Mary, Chapter 4
**Agent:** EMET (Literal/Transparent)
**Source:** P.Berol. 8502, Gospel of Mary, p. 7 (partial) | Coptic
**Chapter:** 4

---

[Pages 1-6 of the manuscript are lost. The surviving manuscript opens at page 7, mid-sentence, in what editors number chapter 4 or the beginning of chapter 5. Only the tail end of this section survives; the chapter opening is lost in the lacuna.]

**4:1** [...]"will matter then be destroyed or not?"

**4:2** The Savior said, "All natures, all formations, all creatures exist in and with one another, and they will be resolved again into their own roots.

**4:3** "For the nature of matter is resolved into the roots of its nature alone.

**4:4** "He who has ears to hear, let him hear."

---

*Translator's Note (EMET):* Coptic: *sōma* / *hylē* — EMET renders *hylē* as "matter" (physical substance). *physis* rendered "nature." The phrase *"he who has ears to hear"* is a Synoptic echo; EMET preserves it as formula.
